issues.description: Duplicated boolean across two enums creates a stringly-typed coupling
issues.detail: `self._enable_vad` is computed by checking `end_of_utterance_mode` against `{FIXED, EXTERNAL}`, but the public API exposes `turn_detection_mode` with the same two values. The mapping between TurnDetectionMode and EndOfUtteranceMode is implicit and lives elsewhere; the data shape is wrong. A single source of truth (one enum, or a derived predicate computed in one place from the public param) would make the algorithm self-evident and prevent drift the next time a mode is added.

issues.description: Default flip is a behavior change buried in a parameter rename
issues.detail: Changing the default `turn_detection_mode` from EXTERNAL to FIXED silently changes who owns endpointing for every existing caller. The changelog mentions it but the data structure gives no migration affordance. Either keep EXTERNAL as default and require callers to opt into FIXED, or make the parameter required so the choice is explicit. Silent default flips are the kind of cleverness that doesn't earn its keep.

issues.description: `split_sentences` is a tri-state bool used as bi-state
issues.detail: `split_sentences: bool | None = None` then `params.split_sentences or False` collapses None and False to the same behavior. If there's no meaningful third state, just type it `bool = False`. The Optional buys nothing and forces every reader to wonder if None means "server default."

issues.description: Frame-type switch papers over a missing data distinction
issues.detail: Swapping `UserStoppedSpeakingFrame` for `VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame` in `process_frame` works, but the warning branch (`if self._enable_vad: warn`) is now unreachable in practice — VAD frames only arrive when external VAD is wired up. The dead branch is a signal that the data structure (which frame means what) is doing the work the conditional pretends to do. Either drop the branch or assert the invariant.

issues.description: Allowlist of config keys is a hand-maintained parallel data structure
issues.detail: `_prepare_config` keeps a literal list of attribute names that must be edited every time a new InputParams field lands. This is the classic case where the data structure (the InputParams model itself) already knows the answer — iterate model fields and copy those that exist on the target config. The current shape guarantees the next contributor will forget an entry.

issues.description: Commented-out metrics call should be deleted or restored, not shuffled
issues.detail: `# await self.start_processing_metrics()` was moved from after the interruption call to before it, still commented out. Either it's load-bearing (uncomment and explain) or it's dead (delete). Moving dead code around is noise that future readers will treat as intentional.

review.summary: The change is small and mostly mechanical — add a FIXED enum value, listen for the more specific VAD frame, surface a `split_sentences` knob. The shape is fine but the data structures are doing less work than they should: two parallel enums (`TurnDetectionMode` and `EndOfUtteranceMode`) duplicate the FIXED/EXTERNAL distinction, a hand-maintained allowlist of config keys mirrors the InputParams model, and a tri-state Optional bool pretends to carry information it doesn't. The default flip from EXTERNAL to FIXED is a real behavior change for every existing caller and deserves more than a changelog line. Decision: TOO-MUCH-FRAMEWORK around config plumbing, WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE for the mode/VAD coupling; the core logic is SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE and fine to ship once the default-flip and mode-coupling are addressed.
